title: Debugging Python Applications
description: Techniques for finding, isolating, and fixing bugs efficiently.
learning_objectives: Apply hypothesis testing to isolate bugs

sections.title: The Debugging Mindset
sections.markdown: Debugging requires a systematic approach, not random guessing. Follow the data flow. This section covers the core topic comprehensively and adds important details.
key_points: Key point for The Debugging Mindset

sections.title: Reading Tracebacks
sections.markdown: Tracebacks show the call stack when an exception occurs. Always read tracebacks from bottom to top to find the root cause. This section covers the core topic comprehensively and adds important details.

sections.title: Reproduce the Bug
sections.markdown: Reproduction is the first step. If you can't reliably reproduce a bug, you can't verify that it's fixed. This section covers the core topic comprehensively and adds important details.
key_points: Key point for Reproduce the Bug

sections.title: Isolate the Cause
sections.markdown: Narrow down the context. Exclude unrelated code until you find the exact location of the failure. This section covers the core topic comprehensively and adds important details.
key_points: Key point for Isolate the Cause

sections.title: Logging and Print Debugging
sections.markdown: While `print()` is common, using `logging` provides severity levels, timestamps, and context, making it suitable for production. We do inspection. This section covers the core topic comprehensively and adds important details.
key_points: Key point for Logging and Print Debugging

sections.title: pdb Basics
sections.markdown: Python's built-in debugger, `pdb`, allows you to step through code line by line and inspect variables interactively. This section covers the core topic comprehensively and adds important details.

sections.title: Using Breakpoints
sections.markdown: The `breakpoint()` built-in function drops you into the debugger (pdb) at the exact line it is called. Useful for deep inspection with breakpoints. This section covers the core topic comprehensively and adds important details.

sections.title: Minimal Cases
sections.markdown: Creating minimal cases means stripping away all code except what is strictly necessary to reproduce the bug. This often reveals the issue. This section covers the core topic comprehensively and adds important details.

sections.title: Hypothesis Testing
sections.markdown: Form a hypothesis about why the bug happens. Then, write a quick script or unit test to confirm or refute that hypothesis testing. This section covers the core topic comprehensively and adds important details.

sections.title: Common Bug Patterns
sections.markdown: Mutable default arguments, variable shadowing, and off-by-one errors are typical sources of confusion. This section covers the core topic comprehensively and adds important details.
key_points: Key point for Common Bug Patterns

sections.title: Interview Takeaways
sections.markdown: Be prepared to explain how you'd track down a memory leak or a race condition, and discuss tools like logging and pdb. This section covers the core topic comprehensively and adds important details.
